subject: Game Theory
title: Bertrand Competition
description: A short lesson to help you apply Bertrand Competition.

hook.text: Two gas stations across the street. Whoever is cheaper gets all the customers. Welcome to Bertrand.

buildup.text: In Bertrand competition, firms compete on price. Each one undercuts the other by a penny.

discovery.text: The equilibrium: both firms price at cost, earning zero profit—even with only two competitors.

twist.text: This 'Bertrand paradox' seems extreme, but gas stations, airlines, and telecoms often slash margins this way.

climax.text: Firms escape Bertrand by differentiating: brand, quality, location, or service justify premium pricing.

punchline.text: Price wars end at zero profit.

quiz.question: What is the Bertrand paradox?
options: Two competitors can drive profits to zero
